reference: GNU ed 1.21.1 (Debian package ed 1.21.1-1, /usr/bin/ed in the runner reference PATH), run black-box and compared for stdout, stderr where marked exact, exit status and the resulting files. The bash type/help cases are contracts on the builtin's own metadata.
coverage: Bash type and help metadata for the static ed builtin and its synopsis/documented command set.
Bash type and help metadata for the ed builtin and its GNU synopsis.
Every existing POSIX case is now compared with GNU ed (parity) instead of a hand-written expectation.
Guest pass 5 G72: addressed a/i/c, g and v, s with \1..\9 and &, the diff -e | ed flow, ?/h/H and exit statuses, -p and -s, l wrapping, missing final newline, unreadable FILE.
GNU ed 1.21.1 script files: standard input that is a regular file stops at the first error.
exclusions: Terminal sessions (prompt echo, interrupts, the modified-buffer warning at a tty) are covered by the parity-vm terminal suites.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify ed as a builtin when PATH is empty.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t ed) == builtin ]]
printf 'builtin\n'

cases.purpose: The Bash help entry shows the GNU ed synopsis and documents the script-file and exit-status rules.
cases.script:
doc=$(help ed)
[[ $doc == *'ed [-EGlqrsv] [-p PROMPT] [--strip-trailing-cr] [FILE | !COMMAND]'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'Edit text with the standard line editor.'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'When standard'*'input is a file, the first error ends ed.'* ]]
printf 'help metadata ok\n'

cases.purpose: POSIX ed append plus n and = commands print line numbers and text in their specified forms.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
alpha
beta
.
1,2n
2=
w sink.txt
q
ED

cases.purpose: POSIX BRE substitution with g and replacement '&' must replace each match with the matched text surrounded by angle brackets.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
id=7 id=42
.
1s/[0-9][0-9]*/<&>/g
1p
w sink.txt
q
ED

cases.purpose: Forward and backward regular-expression addresses wrap through the buffer, and a marked line remains addressable.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
red
blue
red
.
1ka
/blue/
?red?
'a
w sink.txt
q
ED

cases.purpose: The r command inserts a relative file after the current line; verify the resulting buffer text.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha\nbeta\n' > payload.txt
ed -s <<'ED'
a
head
.
r payload.txt
1,$p
w sink.txt
q
ED

cases.purpose: The w command creates a relative fixture file from the buffer; read it back with Bash builtins to verify bytes as lines.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
north
south
.
w saved.txt
q
ED
while IFS= read -r line; do printf '%s\n' "$line"; done < saved.txt

cases.purpose: Undo restores the line before the most recent substitution; the saved clean state also permits a normal quit.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
before
.
w saved.txt
s/before/after/
u
1p
q
ED

cases.purpose: The t command copies an addressed range after the destination, j joins addressed lines without a separator, and w persists the final buffer.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
red
blue
green
.
1,2t$
1,$p
4,5j
1,$p
w final.txt
q
ED
while IFS= read -r line; do printf 'file:%s\n' "$line"; done < final.txt

cases.purpose: Check the editor's modified-buffer quit warning and response while attached to a terminal.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a bounded PTY driver that can send ed commands and capture the prompt/response sequence. The current runner provides no terminal fixture; any future fixture must use only relative files inside its private workspace.

cases.purpose: POSIX BRE replacement offsets and beginning-of-line anchors remain relative to the original line.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
xx1 y22 z333
.
1s/[0-9][0-9]*/<&>/g
1p
w output.txt
q
ED
[[ $(<output.txt) == "xx<1> y<22> z<333>" ]]

cases.purpose: POSIX BRE replacement offsets and beginning-of-line anchors remain relative to the original line.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
abc
.
1s/^/X/g
1p
w output.txt
q
ED
[[ $(<output.txt) == "Xabc" ]]

cases.script:

two
three
four

' > f

A
.
0a
Z
.
$a
E
.
2i
I
.
4c
C
.
,n
w
q
' | ed -s f
printf '%s
' "$(<f)"

cases.purpose: G72: g/RE/cmd and v/RE/cmd run on matching and non-matching lines; a g list continued with backslashes.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
' > f
printf 'g/o/s/o/0/
v/0/s/$/!/
g/^/s/^/>/\
s/$/</
,p
Q
' | ed -s f

cases.purpose: G72: \1..\9 and & in s replacements, a count and g, and \N beyond the groups is the digit.
G72: the diff -e a b | ed flow applies change, delete and append hunks, including lines that are a lone dot.
cases.script:
printf '1
2
3
4
5
6
7
' > a
printf '1
.
3
..
new
6
7
8
' > b
diff -e a b > s || true
(cat s; echo w) | ed -s a
[[ $(<a) == "$(<b)" ]]
printf 'applied
'

cases.purpose: G72: errors print ?, H explains each, h the last; a failed command makes the status 1 and a modified buffer at end of input 2.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
' > f
printf '9p
h
H
zz
1,2j
q
' | ed -s f || echo rc=$?
printf '2d
' | ed -s f || echo rc=$?
printf '2d
' | ed -ls f || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: GNU ed 1.21.1: with standard input a regular file the first error ends ed (status 1) and H names the script line; earlier writes stay.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
' > f
printf '2d
w
H
1p
99p
2p
' > sc
ed -s f < sc || echo rc=$?
printf '%s
' "$(<f)"

cases.purpose: -p sets the prompt shown before each command; without -s the byte counts are printed.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
' > f
printf '1
P
2
$=
w g
q
' | ed -p '* ' f

cases.purpose: l escapes control and non-ASCII bytes and wraps at 76 columns as GNU ed 1.21.1 does.
cases.script:
{ printf 'x%.0s' {1..170}; printf '
	\001\177\303\251\end
'; } > f
printf ',l
,n
Q
' | ed -s f

cases.purpose: A file without a final newline: Newline appended is printed unless -s, and w writes the newline.
cases.script:
printf 'a
b' > f
printf 'w g
q
' | ed f
printf 'q
' | ed -s f

cases.purpose: GNU ed 1.21.1: a directory operand is reported on standard error (no ?), status 1; a missing one is a new file.
cases.script:
mkdir d
printf 'q
' | ed d || echo rc=$?
printf 'a
x
.
w
q
' | ed -s new
printf '%s
' "$(<new)"
